ai.description: This slender colubrid reaches 100–120 cm. It is vibrant green with a thin, dark postocular stripe and a pale venter. Distinctive features include a keeled dorsal scale texture and a pointed snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gonyosoma prasinum* is best distinguished by its uniform, vibrant green body lacking the distinct black-edged scales or bold lateral stripes found on similar green snakes.
ai.habitat: *Gonyosoma prasinum* inhabits dense, humid evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Indian subcontinent, typically found at elevations between 500 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Green Trinket Snake is primarily diurnal and arboreal, often remaining motionless among foliage to ambush small prey or evade detection through its cryptic coloration.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gonyosoma prasinum* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 3–8 eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months, roughly from April to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Gonyosoma prasinum* is found in Northeast India (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Nagaland) within the Eastern Himalayas, typically inhabiting elevations from 300 to 2,000 meters.
